value: species-specific terminal frequency 46.5 kHz for signals of 5.5 ms duration
method: calls recorded with a horizontally oriented T-shaped planar array of four microphones; duration, pulse interval, peak frequency and terminal frequency measured; species-level value calculated from 43 sound sequences with 2147 echolocation calls
conditions: wild, free-flying foraging common pipistrelles at Bebenhausen and Ofterdingen, Baden-Wuerttemberg, Germany, July to October 2010; the number of bats is unknown (stated by the authors), sex and age not reported; individual terminal frequencies at 5.5 ms are reported to fall between about 43.5 and 49.1 kHz

source.authors: Götze S, Koblitz JC, Denzinger A, Schnitzler HU
source.title: No evidence for spectral jamming avoidance in echolocation behavior of foraging pipistrelle bats

where: Results, Echolocation behavior and transmission channels of single flying bats
quote: The calculated average species-specific terminal frequency of signals with duration of 5.5 ms was 46.5 kHz.
note: The value is a calculated average at a fixed call duration of 5.5 ms, not a raw mean of all calls. The paper reports terminal frequency; it gives no peak-frequency value in the sections read. The study tested jamming avoidance and found frequency changes independent of the frequency difference between bats (null result for spectral jamming avoidance); this record is baseline call structure only. Authors from the Crossref record and the Tuebingen repository byline (the nature.com page showed a truncated list). measurement: total myelinated axons of the cochlear nerve, mean +/- SD (the lowest of the seven shrew and mole species examined)
units: myelinated axons per cochlear nerve (mean; SD 125)
method: cochlear nerve imaged in semi-thin sections by light microscopy and axons counted manually from montages (method as filed by d325 for the same paper; the Methods were not re-read here)
conditions: animals described as wild-caught in live traps (Pennsylvania animals in Potter and Cameron Counties; the page text read did not tie the smoky shrews to a site); sex and age not stated; number of individuals counted not given in the text read (per-species values are in Table S2, not read)

source.authors: Leitch DB, Sarko DK, Catania KC
source.title: Brain Mass and Cranial Nerve Size in Shrews and Moles

quote: The total number of myelinated axons of the cochlear nerve varied significantly … with the greatest number of axons found in the Eastern mole … and the fewest in the smoky shrew (mean = 5865, Std dev. = 125) …
